subject: Storage horizon Q&A — prompts, model outputs, transient request handling
messages:
From: John Doe <john.doe@brightbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on what you keep and for how long

Hi Kimberly,

We're compiling a short FAQ for our security review and I hit a couple of gray areas in Redwood's retention model. Can you confirm the default storage horizon for the following artifact types under the hosted API?

- Raw requests / user inputs (prompts)
- Model responses / generated outputs (final completions)
- Streamed fragments / interim tokens (during streaming)
- KV cache / session state (short-lived model state)

Specifically: what is the default retention window (days), whether items are classified as "ephemeral" vs "archived" by default, and what the erasure path looks like (customer-requested erase + evidence). We don't need legal wording — just a clear engineering-level explanation so I can include it in the BrightBank security pack.

Also, if there are common exceptions (e.g., for telemetry, debugging, or legal hold), call those out.

Thanks,
John
John Doe
BrightBank — InfoSec
[attachment: security_qna_template.docx]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what you keep and for how long

John — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise engineering summary you can drop into the pack. Let me know if you want a one-line table instead.

---
Executive summary (hosted API, default config):

- Raw requests / prompts: retained 30 days by default. Prompts are classified as captured request artifacts. They are searchable in internal debug tooling for the retention window and subject to customer erasure requests.

- Final model outputs / completions: retained 30 days by default. Outputs are treated as generated artifacts and follow the same default preservation window for troubleshooting and quality monitoring.

- Streamed fragments / interim tokens: treated as ephemeral; by default streaming buffers are flushed and not persisted beyond the session unless the session is explicitly finalized. If a streamed session is finalized and marked for capture, only the final completion is stored (not every intermediate fragment).

- KV cache / session state: short-lived, typically TTL of 24 hours in the runtime; caches are not persisted to long-term object storage in the hosted default. If a customer enables session archival, that becomes a configuration option with clear consent and a separate retention setting.

Exceptions & notes:

- Telemetry / operational logs: separate retention policy (analytics/observability). By default telemetry is retained 90 days; debug traces associated with a customer can be retained longer on request for investigations, with legal/ops approval.

- Legal holds / audit requests: retention windows can be extended for the duration of a legal hold; erasure is paused while the hold applies.

- Customer-configured retention: Dedicated/Private customers can override defaults via configuration or contract (e.g., 0-day capture for prompts). These are non-default deployments and require SOW/contract terms.

Erasure path (customer-initiated):

1) Customer requests erasure via support portal or API.
2) Operations validates scope (thread id / timeframe).
3) Data marked for deletion is tombstoned immediately in index and scheduled for background purge from object stores.
4) Deletion completion and proof-of-deletion artifacts (deletion job id, timestamp, affected keys) are provided as evidence within 48 hours.

Attached: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (compact table you can paste) and a short excerpt of the erasure runbook.

Hope that helps — happy to jump on a 15-minute call if the pack needs more formality.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
[attachment: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@brightbank.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what you keep and for how long

Adding two practical examples to make the FAQ less abstract (feel free to include these in the pack):

- Conversational bot A (default hosted): user prompt + final answer stored for 30 days; streamed transcripts not stored. If Bank wants no storage of prompts, we can enable "no-capture" at the API key level — that setting prevents prompts and outputs from being saved.

- Analytics trial (debug enabled): when debug trace is turned on for a session we capture full request/response pairs for 90 days to allow model regression triage; traces are tagged and access-controlled.

Kimberly: can you confirm the exact text to use for the "no-capture" toggle? I want to avoid implying it deletes existing data retroactively.

—Marissa
Product Manager, Data Governance
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what you keep and for how long

John / team — quick add from compliance:

- "No-capture" toggle: prevents any new request/response pairs from being saved from the moment it is enabled. It does not retroactively delete artifacts captured prior to toggle activation. For retroactive erasure, use the erasure API/support path described above.

- Proof-of-deletion SLA: we commit to providing deletion evidence within 48 hours of a validated request for hosted customers (subject to legal hold exceptions).

Kimberly / Marissa: looks good to me. John — if you'd like formalized language for the vendor security questionnaire we can prepare a short appendix (1 paragraph + 1 table) using the spreadsheet Kimberly attached.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Compliance & Privacy
Redwood Inference
